name: LM5175RHFR
title: 42 V wide-input synchronous four-switch buck-boost controller
summary: The LM5175 controls a single-inductor, four-switch buck-boost converter that can hold its output above, below or equal to the input, from 3.5 V to 42 V in (60 V absolute) to 0.8 V to 55 V out. It drives four external N-channel MOSFETs with integrated gate drivers and uses valley current mode in buck and peak current mode in boost, with one sense resistor in the low-side return. Frequency is set from 100 kHz to 600 kHz by a resistor, can be locked to a clock or dithered, and the part adds soft-start, UVLO, power good, output OVP, optional hiccup, optional average input or output current limit, CCM/DCM selection and thermal shutdown. It comes in HTSSOP-28 and VQFN-28.

circuits.title: Four-switch buck-boost, 6 V to 36 V in, 12 V at 6 A out
circuits.description: A 300 kHz four-switch converter holding 12 V at up to 6 A from a 6 V to 36 V source. QH1 and QL1 form the input half-bridge on SW1, QH2 and QL2 the output half-bridge on SW2, with the 4.7 µH inductor between the two switch nodes. Both low-side sources return through the 8 mΩ RSENSE, read through 100 Ω / 47 pF filters at CS and CSG. Schottky diodes from VCC charge the 0.1 µF bootstrap capacitors. The controller's own VIN pin is fed through a series diode and a 10 Ω / 0.1 µF filter, while VISNS sees the input rail directly. BIAS and VOSNS take power and sense from the output. A 0 Ω part sits in the average-current sense position between the output ceramics and the bulk output capacitors, filtered by 100 Ω resistors and 1 µF into ISNS(+) and ISNS(-). 249 kΩ over 59.0 kΩ sets the UVLO, 280 kΩ over 20 kΩ sets 12 V on FB, 84.5 kΩ on RT/SYNC sets 300 kHz, and a 1 nF capacitor couples an optional external clock. 93.1 kΩ on MODE picks CCM with hiccup; DITH is grounded, so dither is off. CSS = 0.1 µF gives about 16 ms of soft-start, CSLOPE = 100 pF sets the slope ramp, and 10 kΩ with 22 nF plus 100 pF compensate the loop.

parts.note: series blocking diode in the VIN pin supply

notes: The MOSFETs and diodes have no part values. QH1 and QL1 see the full input plus switching spikes and are rated 60 V; QH2 and QL2 see the 12 V output plus spikes and are rated 20 V or more.
AGND and PGND share one ground. The DITH connection to ground may be a 0 Ω resistor.

operation.text: Synchronous four-switch buck-boost controller for one inductor, with drivers for four external N-channel MOSFETs. When VIN is above VOUT it runs as a buck, below VOUT as a boost, and near VOUT in a proprietary transition mode that keeps output ripple low without losing efficiency. Input range 3.5 V to 42 V (60 V absolute), output 0.8 V to 55 V.

One die in two 28-pin packages: HTSSOP (PWP, 9.7 mm × 4.4 mm body) as LM5175PWP and VQFN (RHF, 4.0 mm × 5.0 mm body) as LM5175RHF. Orderable numbers differ only in package, reel quantity and the G4/.A/.B suffixes; all are rated -40 °C to 125 °C. An AEC-Q100 automotive version, LM5175-Q1, also exists.

Fixed-frequency current-mode control. The divided output on FB is compared with VREF by a transconductance error amplifier driving COMP; the sensed CS-CSG voltage plus an adaptive slope ramp built from VIN, VOUT and the SLOPE capacitor is compared with COMP. In buck mode the control is valley current mode: HDRV1 turns on when the inductor current falls to its valley and the clock turns it off, which suits very short on-times. In boost mode it is peak current mode: the clock turns on LDRV2 and the comparator turns it off at the peak. LDRV1 is the complement of HDRV1 and HDRV2 the complement of LDRV2.
Peak current mode needs slope compensation above 50% duty and valley mode below 50%. One capacitor on SLOPE sets the ramp for any combination of VIN and VOUT.

VCC, about 7.5 V, feeds the gate drivers and internal rails. It turns on once EN/UVLO passes the standby threshold (0.7 V typical); below 7.5 V of input it follows VIN with a small drop. Switching starts when EN/UVLO is above 1.23 V and VCC is above its 3.3 V undervoltage threshold. With no BIAS supply the regulator runs from VIN; a source on BIAS at least a diode drop above VCC takes over. Tying BIAS to VOUT when VOUT is above 8.5 V raises buck-mode efficiency. BIAS should not go above 36 V. If VIN can sag below what VCC needs, power BIAS from another supply and put a blocking diode in series with VIN so VCC cannot back-feed VIN through the regulator's body diode. VCC needs 1 µF to PGND.

EN/UVLO has three ranges. Below the standby threshold the part is shut down. Between standby and the 1.23 V operating threshold the bias rails and VCC run while SS is held low and the PWM is off; a 1.5 µA current out of the pin gives hysteresis between shutdown and standby. Above 1.23 V, and with VCC above 3.3 V, the controller runs, and an extra 3.5 µA hysteresis current flows so a slow, noisy input does not make it chatter. A divider from VIN to AGND with its tap on EN/UVLO sets the input turn-on level.

An internal 5 µA source charges the SS capacitor. While SS is below 0.8 V it, not VREF, sets the regulated FB voltage. SS is discharged when EN/UVLO drops below the operating threshold, when VCC drops below its UV level, in hiccup and in thermal shutdown. The average current loop also pulls SS down to limit current.

In buck mode the CS-to-CSG valley voltage is clamped at 76 mV: if it does not fall below that during the off time, the high-side switch skips a cycle. In boost mode the peak is limited to 170 mV; reaching it ends the boost switch's on-time for that cycle. With hiccup selected on MODE, 128 consecutive cycles in current limit shut the controller down and discharge SS; it restarts after 4000 clock cycles. Without hiccup it stays in cycle-by-cycle limiting as long as the overload lasts.

operation.topic: Average input or output current limit
operation.text: An extra sense resistor in series with the input or the output feeds ISNS(+) and ISNS(-). A transconductance amplifier compares its drop with 50 mV and, above that, slowly discharges SS; once SS is below 0.8 V the output voltage falls until the current is held. This gives a constant-current behaviour, for example for battery charging. Shorting ISNS(+) to ISNS(-) disables it.

MODE selects the light-load behaviour. In CCM the inductor current may reverse and the frequency stays fixed at any load, which eases filtering in noise-sensitive designs. In DCM the synchronous switches act as diodes: LDRV1 or HDRV2 turns off for the rest of the cycle when the inductor current reaches zero, so the frequency drops at light load and efficiency rises.

A resistor from RT/SYNC to AGND sets 100 kHz to 600 kHz. An external clock can be AC-coupled into RT/SYNC through a capacitor; it must be faster than the RT frequency, with pulses 75 ns to 500 ns wide, and the pin must not see more than 3.3 V peak.

A capacitor from DITH to AGND carries a triangle centred on 1.22 V that moves the oscillator ±5% around the RT frequency. A smaller capacitor modulates faster; the modulation rate must stay far below Fsw to cut peak EMI. DITH tied to AGND gives a fixed frequency, and dither is off whenever an external SYNC clock is used.
The gate drives turn off when FB rises 7.5% above 0.8 V (0.86 V) and switching resumes once the output is back within 5% of VREF.
PGOOD is an open-drain output that pulls low when FB is outside -9% / +10% of 0.8 V. Its pull-down is typically 4.2 mA, and it may be pulled up to a supply of up to 8 V.

COMP swings from 0.3 V to 3 V. Type II compensation is Rc1 in series with Cc1 from COMP to ground, usually with Cc2 across them for a high-frequency pole. The COMP range limits the usable input range: in buck mode the highest VIN for regulation at no load is where COMP reaches 0.3 V, and in boost mode the lowest VIN at full load is where it reaches 3 V. More inductance, a larger CSLOPE, a smaller RSENSE and a higher frequency widen both limits.

Two floating high-side drivers (HDRV1, HDRV2) and two ground-referenced low-side drivers (LDRV1, LDRV2). Each driver sources 1.5 A and sinks 2 A peak (1.8 A and 2.2 A typical at VBOOT - VSW = 7 V). In buck mode LDRV1 and HDRV1 switch and HDRV2 stays on; in boost mode LDRV2 and HDRV2 switch and HDRV1 stays on. In DCM buck LDRV1 and HDRV2 both turn off at zero inductor current; in DCM boost HDRV2 does. HDRV2 stays off during soft-start so a pre-biased output cannot drive current backwards. The low-side drivers run from VCC; the high-side drivers from CBOOT1 (BOOT1 to SW1) and CBOOT2 (BOOT2 to SW2), each charged from VCC through an external Schottky diode.
Above about 165 °C junction the drivers stop and SS is discharged. The converter starts again after the junction cools by the 15 °C hysteresis.
MODE sets CCM or DCM and hiccup on or off, and is latched at start-up.

operation.topic: Design example: frequency and output voltage
operation.text: For 300 kHz, RT = 84.5 kΩ (1%). The output divider uses RFB1 = 20 kΩ to ground and RFB2 = 280 kΩ for 12 V.

The buck case (40% ripple at 36 V) calls for 11.1 µH and the boost case (40% ripple at 6 V) for 2.1 µH. More inductance means less ripple but a bigger part and a lower right-half-plane zero, which lowers the reachable bandwidth; 4.7 µH is the compromise chosen. The peak current at 6 V in is 14.4 A, and with ±20% current-limit tolerance the inductor saturation current should exceed 21.6 A.

In boost mode the output capacitor carries large ripple current (6 A RMS in the example), and in buck mode the input capacitor does (3 A RMS at D = 0.5). Both use a mix of ceramic and bulk capacitors: low ESR and short high-di/dt loops from the ceramics, ripple-current capacity from the bulk parts.

RSENSE between CS and CSG must allow full load in both modes with margin: 8.8 mΩ for buck and 8.2 mΩ for boost, so 8 mΩ is used. It dissipates up to 1.8 W at the lowest input, so a 2 W or larger part is used. An RC filter in the CS and CSG lines may be added against noise; the filter resistors should be 100 Ω or less.

operation.topic: Design example: slope, UVLO, soft-start, dither
operation.text: 235 pF of slope capacitance gives dead-beat current-loop response; half that slope (twice the capacitance) is still stable in theory. 100 pF is used for cleaner behaviour near VIN = VOUT while still covering the input range. RUV2 = 249 kΩ gives 0.8 V of UVLO hysteresis and RUV1 = 59.0 kΩ a turn-on below 6 V; at low UVLO settings the MOSFET gate plateau must sit below the lowest input. CSS = 0.1 µF gives 16 ms. Dither is not used.

The input-side QH1 and QL1 see up to 36 V plus switching spikes on SW1 and are rated 60 V. The output-side QH2 and QL2 see 12 V plus spikes on SW2 and are rated 20 V or more. Gate plateau voltages must be below the lowest input voltage, or the MOSFETs may not enhance fully during start-up or overload. A lower RDSON usually comes with slower edges and more switching loss.

The loop is designed for both buck and boost and the stricter result kept; with deep operation in both regions that is usually boost, because of its right-half-plane zero. In the example the boost RHP zero is 16.9 kHz, so the target crossover is 4 kHz, the compensation zero 600 Hz, and Rc1 = 10 kΩ, Cc1 = 22 nF, Cc2 = 100 pF are used. Placing the zero at three times the buck output pole costs about 30° of phase before buck crossover and 15° at middle frequencies in boost. The final values need tuning on the bench.
Any DC source within the input range, able to supply the highest boost-mode inductor current. An electrolytic capacitor at the board's input damps ringing caused by the supply leads.

Keep CIN, QH1, QL1 and RSENSE tight to minimise the buck input switching loop, and COUT, QH2, QL2 and RSENSE tight for the boost output loop. Use bulk plus small ceramic capacitors on both sides, with the ceramics nearest the IC. SW1 and SW2 are high dv/dt nodes; keep their loop areas small. Join the CIN, COUT and RSENSE grounds closely with wide copper on several layers.

Route each gate drive and its return together, side by side or stacked on adjacent layers, to keep inductance low. Kelvin-connect CS and CSG to RSENSE and run them as a parallel pair to the IC, away from SW1, SW2 and the high-side gate traces; the sense filter capacitor goes at the IC pins.

Place the 1 µF VCC capacitor between VCC and PGND, the 0.1 µF BIAS capacitor between BIAS and PGND, and each bootstrap capacitor straight across BOOT1-SW1 and BOOT2-SW2, all near the IC. Bypass VIN to AGND with a 0.1 µF ceramic close by; with external BIAS, add a diode from the input rail to VIN against reverse conduction when VIN < VCC. Run the feedback divider from the COUT positive terminal to AGND with its parts by FB. Keep power and switching current out of AGND, which would disturb COMP, SLOPE and SYNC or offset FB; join PGND and AGND near the PGND pin, the VCC capacitor ground or the sense resistor ground.
Split CIN or COUT between both sides of the average-current sense resistor to keep its cycle-by-cycle ripple small, and put the ISNS filter capacitor across ISNS(+) and ISNS(-) near the IC.
